en: The Jātaka:
The Fifth Collection, Chapter on the Jeweled Earrings (Maṇikuṇḍalavagga)
7. The Laṭukika Jātaka “I pay homage to you, O elephant of sixty years,
forest-dweller, lord of the herd, renowned for your glory.”
With my wings I pay homage to you with palms joined;
do not kill my young ones, who are so weak.
"I bow to you, O solitary elephant," he said.
“Roaming the mountain ridges in the forest,
I place my wings together in añjali before you;
do not kill my two young ones, for I am weak.”
“I will kill your little ones, little quail;
what can you do to me, for you are weak?
Even hundreds or thousands of such as you—”
I would crush him with my left foot.
“One should not always act with force;
for force leads to the destruction of the fool.”
“I shall do you harm, O king of serpents,
you who slew my two young sons while I was weak.
“Behold the crow and the little lizard!”
The frog and the blue fly—
these two struck down the naga.
Behold the enemy of the enemy!
Therefore, one should indeed not harbor enmity toward anyone,
even toward those who are unpleasant.
Thus ends the seventh Jātaka, the Laṭukika Jātaka.
